speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You've presented with a headache and worsening vision over three weeks; to start my evaluation, please describe exactly how the vision changes occur and whether you have any fever, neck stiffness, or recent head trauma.

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Intracranial Mass (e.g., Brain Tumor or Metastasis)

Please describe the specific nature of your vision changes—such as blurring, double vision, or loss of peripheral vision—and let me know if the headache is worse in the morning or with exertion. I will also need to request a CT scan of the head to evaluate for mass effect or hydrocephalus.
